# RockshinOps

> Free, MIT-licensed desktop toolkit with system monitoring, app and file search, and macOS menu-bar management.

RockshinOps reads native CPU, memory, disk, network, process and connection data. It provides a global-shortcut Launcher with local app/filename search and Chinese pinyin matching, persistent menu bar metrics, developer port inspection, disk-space analysis and reviewed cleanup. Launcher is off by default; file search is optional and skips other apps’ private folders. History stays in memory for the current session; no cloud account is required. Menu-bar icon management (visible/hidden/always-hidden groups, drag sorting, search and temporary reveal) and app-uninstall review are macOS features. The current published download is v0.2.12. On macOS, dedicated Sensors and Devices pages show hardware temperatures, fan readings, Wi-Fi information and requested scans, paired Bluetooth devices and audio output controls. Hardware readings and device controls depend on macOS permissions and device support. Website screenshots use application components with synthetic demonstration data. Hardware telemetry and desktop acceptance vary by platform; see the product pages for limits.
